subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Mineral exploration: geophysical methods for base metal exploration:
options: No geophysical method can detect base-metal sulfides beneath conductive overburden
EM (electromagnetic) methods detect conductive massive sulfides
Gravity methods, because sulfide orebodies lack any magnetic or electrical response
Magnetic methods, as all base-metal sulfides are strongly ferrimagnetic
solution: EM: time-domain or frequency-domain. Massive sulfides: good conductors. Detectable at depth.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In accuracy assessment of a classified satellite image, which statement about the Kappa coefficient is correct?
options: It measures only the producer's accuracy of a single land-cover class
It measures agreement between the classified map and ground truth after correcting for chance agreement
It is numerically identical to the overall accuracy for every confusion matrix
It is computed only for unsupervised classification outputs
solution: Kappa (κ) = (observed agreement − chance agreement)/(1 − chance agreement), computed from the error/confusion matrix. κ > 0.8 indicates strong agreement; it corrects for agreement that would occur by chance.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In a dip-slip fault, movement occurs along which direction, and what are the two resulting fault types?
options: Movement along the strike direction with no vertical component involved
Pure rotational movement about a vertical axis with no translation at all
Movement along dip direction (normal or reverse)
Oblique movement combining equal strike and dip components on the fault
solution: Dip-slip: vertical component. Oblique-slip: both dip and strike components.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An opencast block of 50000 m² has 50 m of overburden above the seam. The overburden volume to be removed is:
options: 0.25 million m³
2.5 million m³
5.0 million m³
1.25 million m³
solution: Volume = area × depth = 50000×50 = 2500000 m³ = 2.5 million m³.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Evaporation is measured with a Class A evaporation pan and converted to lake evaporation using:
options: Class A evaporation pan. Pan coefficient (0.7-0.8) to convert to lake evaporation
Direct measurement of the total volume of water lost from the surface of the lake by evaporation
Pan evaporation readings that require no conversion factor of any kind to be applied
Measurement of the evaporation losses using a standard recording rain gauge instrument
solution: Class A pan: 1.2m diameter, 0.25m deep. Pan evaporation > lake evaporation (K_p).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In rock mass classification, the Geological Strength Index (GSI) estimates which property used as input to the Hoek-Brown failure criterion?
options: Intact rock compressive strength
Rock mass quality based on blockiness and joint surface condition
Porosity of the intact rock material
In-situ stress magnitude at depth
solution: GSI (Hoek-Brown criterion) estimates rock mass strength from the structure (blockiness) and joint surface condition; it correlates with RMR and Q systems and is used with the Hoek-Brown failure criterion for slopes and tunnels.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Convergent, divergent and transform plate boundaries represent which classification of interactions between lithospheric plates?
options: Plate boundaries consist only of convergent margins where plates collide with one another
Plate boundaries consist only of divergent margins where plates move apart from one another
Plate boundaries consist only of transform margins where plates slide horizontally past one another without creating or destroying crust
Convergent (subduction/collision), Divergent (spreading), Transform (strike-slip)
solution: Tectonic plates: 7 major (Pacific, N.Am, S.Am, Africa, Eurasia, Australia, Antarctica). Move cm/yr.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) in remote sensing:
options: Increases the number of bands by creating additional synthetic channels of data output
Reduces correlated bands to uncorrelated components. PC1 = maximum variance
Adds false colour composites to the image, in order to improve the visual interpretation of it
Simply reorders the original bands, without changing any of their numerical values at all
solution: PCA: dimensionality reduction. PC1: brightness. PC2: contrast. PC3: noise usually.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following is a typical stratabound, carbonate-hosted Pb-Zn deposit formed by warm basinal brines?
options: Porphyry copper deposit
Mississippi Valley-Type (MVT) Pb-Zn deposit
Podiform chromite in ophiolite
Pegmatite-hosted lithium deposit
solution: MVT deposits: stratabound Pb-Zn hosted in carbonate platforms, precipitated by warm basinal brines (e.g., Zawar, Rajasthan). SEDEX deposits are similar but synsedimentary and hosted in shale.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which sequence records oceanic crust: peridotite, gabbro, sheeted dykes, pillow basalt, chert?
options: Continental crust section composed of gneisses, schists and granite plutons beneath mountain belts
Granite batholith with its associated pegmatite and aplite dyke swarms
Volcanic arc sequence built of andesite lavas and pyroclastic deposits
Oceanic crust sequence: peridotite → gabbro → sheeted dykes → pillow basalt → chert
solution: Ophiolite: obducted oceanic lithosphere. Troodos (Cyprus), Oman.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Geological time scale divisions (largest to smallest):
options: Only the two finest divisions, Epoch and Age, are formally recognised
Eon, Era, Period, Epoch, Age
Age, Epoch, Period, Era, Eon when arranged from the smallest to the largest
Random order that varies from one geological region to another in the world
solution: Eon: Precambrian, Phanerozoic. Era: Paleozoic, Mesozoic, Cenozoic. Period: Cambrian, etc.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How is porosity in sedimentary rocks classified, and what processes generate each type?
options: Porosity related only to the size and shape of sedimentary structures
Only secondary porosity, with all primary depositional porosity completely absent
Primary (depositional) vs secondary (diagenetic: dissolution, fracturing)
Only primary porosity, with no secondary dissolution or fracture porosity present
solution: Sandstone: intergranular porosity. Carbonates: vuggy, moldic, fracture porosity.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Well log correlation: gamma ray log identifies:
options: Porosity from the neutron hydrogen index at any depth
Fluid resistivity and water saturation of the logged interval
Matrix density and acoustic travel time for secondary porosity
Shale content (high GR = shale, low GR = sand/carbonate)
solution: GR: natural radioactivity. K, U, Th. Shale: high GR. Sand: low GR. Clean carbonate: low GR.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A dipping coal seam outcrops over a horizontal width of 50 m on flat ground and dips at 50°. Its true thickness is about:
solution: True thickness = horizontal width × sin(dip) = 50×sin50° ≈ 38.3 m.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In the Jacob straight-line method of aquifer test analysis, drawdown is plotted against log time on:
options: Straight-line on semilog plot. s = (2.303Q)/(4πT)·log(2.25Tt/(r²S))
Match the observed field data to a type curve of W(u) against the 1/u values
Bouwer-Rice analysis of slug recovery for the same test data set
Hvorslev analysis of the initial water level in the observation well of the test
solution: Jacob: t₀ from s=0 intercept. T = 2.303Q/(4π·Δs). S = 2.25T·t₀/r².

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Natural levees, backswamps, oxbow lakes, yazoo streams and crevasse splays are characteristic features of which environment?
options: The floodplain contains only natural levee deposits along the banks
The floodplain contains only abandoned meander loops or oxbow lakes
The floodplain contains only crevasse splays formed during major flood events
Natural levee, backswamp, oxbow lake, yazoo stream, crevasse splay
solution: Floodplain: flat area adjacent to river, periodically flooded. Alluvial soil.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is an intrusive igneous body smaller than a batholith (<100 km²)?
options: Igneous body that is exactly the same size as a batholith in outcrop area
Intrusion larger than a batholith extending over hundreds of square km
Volcanic landform built of lava flows and pyroclastic material around a vent
Smaller than batholith (<100 km²)
solution: Stock: similar to batholith but smaller. Often associated with mineral deposits.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which sequence correctly shows the progressive metamorphic grade sequence for pelitic rocks?
options: Schist→Slate→Phyllite→Gneiss (decreasing grade)
Gneiss→Schist→Slate→Phyllite (reverse order)
Phyllite→Slate→Schist→Gneiss (starting with phyllite)
Slate→Phyllite→Schist→Gneiss→Migmatite
solution: Increasing T/P. Slate (low), phyllite (sheen), schist (crystals visible), gneiss (bands).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Evapotranspiration is the combined process of water loss from the soil and vegetation, and its reference rate (ETo) is estimated from:
options: The loss of water only from the surface of open water bodies and bare soil
Combined evaporation + transpiration. Reference ET (ETo) from weather data
The release of water vapour only through the leaves and stomata of plants
The downward movement of water through the soil profile into the groundwater table below
solution: Penman-Monteith: ETo = (0.408Δ(R_n-G)+γ·900/(T+273)u₂(e_s-e_a))/(Δ+γ(1+0.34u₂)).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How do stone columns improve the engineering behaviour of soft ground?
options: Cement grouting of the soil to form a rigid continuous mass beneath the structure
Vibro-replacement. Granular columns improve bearing capacity and drainage
Soil nailing of the slope face without any ground densification
Deep mixing with lime slurry to stabilize the entire soil layer
solution: Stone columns: 0.6-1.1m diameter. Install by vibroflot. Reduce liquefaction. Increase BC 2-3×.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Arranged from lowest to highest rank, the coal series is:
options: Anthracite → bituminous → lignite → peat
Peat → lignite → bituminous → anthracite
Bituminous → anthracite → peat → lignite
Lignite → peat → anthracite → bituminous
solution: Increasing rank (carbon content) goes peat, lignite, sub-bituminous/bituminous, anthracite.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the seismic refraction method primarily used to determine?
options: S-wave velocity of the deeper mantle beneath the continental crust
Electrical conductivity to locate ore bodies and mineral veins
Magnetic anomalies produced by the iron-rich rocks below
P-wave velocity. Depth to bedrock, rippability
solution: Seismic: hammer or explosives. Higher Vp = harder rock. Refraction for shallow (<30m).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A 3 m seam over 6 km² (density 1.4 t/m³) has a recovery factor of 0.75. The mineable reserve is about:
solution: Mineable = area×thickness×density×recovery = 6M m²×3×1.4×0.75 ≈ 18.9 Mt.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In tectonic stress analysis, what do the three principal stress symbols σ₁, σ₂ and σ₃ respectively represent?
options: σ₁ < σ₂ < σ₃, with σ₃ representing the maximum principal stress in the system
σ₁ = σ₂ = σ₃, so stress is equal in all directions and no shear acts on any plane
σ₁ = σ₃ at failure, so the two horizontal stresses are always equal in value
σ₁ > σ₂ > σ₃. Maximum, intermediate, minimum principal stresses
solution: Anderson: σ₁ vertical (normal faults), σ₂ vertical (strike-slip), σ₃ vertical (thrust).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Using a simplified proxy where calorific value ≈ 70 × fixed-carbon%, a coal with 60% fixed carbon has a calorific value of about:
options: 8400 kcal/kg
4900 kcal/kg
2100 kcal/kg
4200 kcal/kg
solution: CV ≈ 70 × 60 = 4200 kcal/kg (illustrative proxy).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Into which two broad types is the lustre of minerals classified in hand specimen study?
options: Only metallic lustre is exhibited by opaque ore minerals such as galena
Metallic (opaque) or non-metallic (vitreous, pearly, silky, earthy)
Body color alone determines the observed mineral lustre
Hardness controls whether a mineral appears dull or bright
solution: Metallic: pyrite, galena. Vitreous: quartz. Pearly: talc. Silky: asbestos.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Specific storage (Ss) of an aquifer is defined as the volume of water released per:
options: The volume of water drained from storage in an aquifer under the pull of gravity alone during the pumping
The ratio of the saturated aquifer thickness to its specific yield value during tests
Volume released per unit volume per unit head change. Elastic (confined). Ss = ρg(α + nβ)
The volume of water released from a confined aquifer by the pull of gravity drainage alone
solution: Ss: compressibility of water (β=4.4×10^-10 Pa^-1) and aquifer (α). Confined: S = Ss×b. Unconfined: S_y.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the chemical formula and structural type of biotite, a mica group mineral?
options: Framework silicate with three-dimensional SiO4 linkage
Tectosilicate structure identical to that of feldspar
Dioctahedral phyllosilicate with two Al per formula unit
K(Mg,Fe)3(AlSi3O10)(OH)2 — trioctahedral
solution: Biotite: black mica. Trioctahedral (3 Mg/Fe per formula unit). Common in many rocks.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The capture zone of a pumping well is defined as the portion of the aquifer from which:
options: Volume of aquifer from which well draws water
The entire area of the aquifer basin feeding the river system
Only the physical volume of the borehole and the pump chamber
The region where water levels rise above the original static level
solution: Capture zone: area of flow lines terminating at well.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal seam covers 5 km², is 2 m thick, with density 1.3 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
options: 10 Mt
26 Mt
6.5 Mt
13 Mt
solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 5×10⁶ m²×2 m×1.3 t/m³ ≈ 13 Mt.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A bed drops 30 m over a horizontal distance of 40 m. Its dip angle is about:
solution: dip = tan⁻¹(rise/run) = tan⁻¹(30/40) ≈ 36.9°.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What streak colour does the mineral pyrite produce when rubbed on a streak plate?
options: Brownish black
Greenish black
Brassy yellow
Dark grey
solution: Pyrite (FeS2) — brassy yellow, greenish-black streak. 'Fool's gold'.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The capillary fringe is the zone lying above the water table where water is held by:
options: Zone below the water table where all the pores are completely filled
Zone above water table where water is held by capillary forces. Saturation > 0
Thin dry layer at the surface that transmits no water to the roots
Saturated band located beneath the aquifer's impermeable confining bed layer at depth
solution: Capillary rise: fine sand 1-2m, silt 2-5m, clay >10m. Negative pressure.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The specific yield (S_y) of an unconfined aquifer is defined as the:
options: Volume drained by gravity / total volume. Unconfined aquifer storage
Ratio of pore water held against gravity to the total volume
Volume of water released per unit surface area per unit head fall
Fraction of the total volume stored as water under confined pressure
solution: S_y: sand 0.2-0.3, clay 0.02-0.05. S_y + S_r = porosity (S_r = specific retention).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What do load casts on the base of a sedimentary bed indicate about their formation?
options: Ridge-like projections found on the top surface of the sandstone bed
Irregular pods confined to the interior of a single thick massive bed
Bulbous projections on bottom of bed. Soft sediment deformation
Straight, parallel ridges aligned exactly with the bedding plane direction
solution: Load cast: differential loading. Flute cast: current scour. Both sole marks (bottom of bed).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which mining method typically produces a subsidence trough at the surface?
options: Subsidence only occurs at the mine portal and never above the extracted panel area
The ground surface always rises as an uplift dome over the panel
Longwall mining → subsidence trough. Angle of draw. Impact on structures
Roof falls underground are fully unrelated to any surface movement
solution: Subsidence: vertical displacement. Tilt and curvature cause damage. Mitigation: backfill, pillars.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which landform is characteristic of the lower course of a river and is formed when a meander loop is cut off and abandoned?
options: Alluvial fan
Oxbow lake
Yardang
Cirque
solution: Oxbow lakes form when a meander neck is breached and the loop is abandoned as a crescent-shaped lake; typical of floodplains in the lower course. Alluvial fans form at mountain fronts.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following is a method of artificial groundwater recharge?
options: Only riverbank filtration of surface water along the banks of the perennial rivers of the region
Check dams, recharge wells, percolation tanks, roof-top harvesting, injection wells
Only the pumping of groundwater from deep production wells during a prolonged drought period of the year
Only seawater intrusion barriers that are built along the coastal belt of the open sea
solution: MAR: aquifer storage and recovery (ASR). Water quality treatment. Clogging management.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The Permian–Triassic mass extinction is attributed mainly to which cause?
options: Siberian Traps volcanism and climate change
Asteroid impact at the K-Pg boundary layer
Global cooling associated with a major ice age
Rapid sea level fall on passive continental margins
solution: P-T extinction: largest in Earth history. ~96% species lost. Caused by Siberian Traps: CO2, SO2, ozone depletion, ocean anoxia.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Ore reserve classification (JORC): indicated resource requires:
options: Sufficient exploration for geological confidence but lower than measured
Surface exposure of the orebody without any sampling carried out beneath it
No drilling, with tonnage estimated purely from regional geological extrapolation
Any level of confidence, including purely speculative regional analogies
solution: Indicated: enough data for planning. Inferred: limited data. Measured: high confidence.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following is a common rockfall protection measure?
options: Only the removal of the source block by controlled blasting of the cliff face
Only warning sirens with no physical protection measure at all
Only regrading of the slope to a gentler uniform angle
Barrier, catch ditch, mesh, rock bolt, shotcrete. Warning systems
solution: Rockfall: netting (draped, anchored). Attenuator barriers. Risk: exposure × probability × consequence.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which mineral pair is the essential assemblage of the eclogite facies at very high pressure?
options: Garnet + omphacite. Very high P. Densest crustal rock (~3.5 g/cm³)
Amphibole-bearing assemblage that is stable at moderate pressures
Low-density quartz-feldspar rock formed at very shallow crustal depths
Hydrous mineral assemblage stable in shallow crustal levels
solution: Eclogite: subduction zone. Coesite in UHP rocks. Diamond-grade: >4 GPa.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following correctly describes pingos, their morphology and the two systems by which they form?
options: Cone-shaped hill built up by repeated eruptions of lava and pyroclastic material around a central volcanic vent
Ridge of wind-blown sand aligned with the prevailing wind direction in a desert region
Ice-cored mounds in permafrost. Open-system (groundwater) and closed-system (lake)
Ridge of unsorted debris deposited along the margin of a glacier during a period of retreat
solution: Pingo: up to 100m high. Collapse pingo → thermokarst pond. Continuous permafrost zone.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the relative duration of the Precambrian, Paleozoic, Mesozoic, and Cenozoic in the geological time scale?
options: All eras are of equal duration across the entire geological time scale of the Earth history
Precambrian is the shortest interval, covering less than 10% of Earth's recorded geological history
Precambrian (88%), Paleozoic (545-251 Ma), Mesozoic (251-66 Ma), Cenozoic (66 Ma-present)
Cenozoic is the longest era, spanning nearly half of the total Earth history span recorded
solution: Hadean, Archean, Proterozoic (Precambrian). Phanerozoic: Paleo-Meso-Cenozoic.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: (U-Th)/He dating of apatite, with a helium closure temperature of about 70°C, is mainly used to study what?
options: Closure at a low temperature of about sixty to seventy degrees centigrade
He diffusion: closure temperature ~70°C. For exhumation studies
No dependence of the helium retention on temperature whatsoever at any depth
Very high closure temperature near three hundred degrees centigrade or more
solution: AHe: low-T thermochronometer. (U-Th)/He age = time since cooling through ~70°C.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In coastal hydrogeology, the Ghyben-Herzberg relation is used to describe which feature of freshwater-saltwater systems?
options: Freshwater-saltwater interface in coastal aquifers
Relationship between rainfall intensity and groundwater recharge
Variation of aquifer thickness with depth below the water table
Rate of seawater movement through a barrier island system
solution: z = 40h. Freshwater head h corresponds to z depth of interface.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An aquifer has hydraulic conductivity 50 m/day and a hydraulic gradient of 0.01. The Darcy velocity is:
options: 5000 m/day
50 m/day
1 m/day
0.5 m/day

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which regions of the electromagnetic spectrum, from visible through near-infrared to microwave, are used in remote sensing?
options: Only the visible and near-infrared portions of the spectrum
Only thermal infrared, used for temperature measurement
Visible (0.4-0.7 μm), NIR, SWIR, TIR, Microwave (radar)
Only microwave, which cannot sense optical properties
solution: Multispectral: multiple bands. Hyperspectral: hundreds of narrow bands.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In a standard False Colour Composite (FCC) displayed with NIR, Red and Green bands, healthy vegetation appears as which colour?
options: Green
Red
Blue
Yellow
solution: In FCC (NIR-Red-Green), healthy vegetation appears red because of its very high near-infrared reflectance; built-up areas appear cyan or grey.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which remote sensing techniques, passive and active, are commonly used to estimate soil moisture from space?
options: Using only optical NDVI vegetation indices, which can directly measure the root-zone water content
Using thermal inertia alone, as derived from a single daytime thermal image only
Passive microwave (L-band: SMOS, SMAP). Active (C-band: Sentinel-1). Optical/thermal
Using only ground-based gravimetry, with no spaceborne sensing involved at all
solution: SMAP: L-band radiometer + radar. 3km, 2-3 day. Soil moisture + freeze/thaw. Surface ~5cm depth.
